svg.aria-label: Diagram: Microsoft Entra activity logs, their contents and their retention. Four activity logs exist: sign-ins, audit, provisioning, and sign-ups which is in preview and for external tenants only. Sign-in logs answer who got in, audit logs record changes applied to the tenant such as user and group management, and provisioning logs record what a connector did between a source and a target system. Entries in the sign-in and provisioning logs are system generated and cannot be changed or deleted. The sign-in logs come in four types: interactive user, non-interactive user, service principal, and managed identity sign-ins, and the legacy sign-in logs experience includes only interactive user sign-ins. A sign-in is described by who, the identity; how, the client application; and what, the target resource. Reading the logs requires at least the Reports Reader role. Retention by licence tier: audit logs and sign-ins are seven days on Free and 30 days on both P1 and P2, so P2 adds no additional retention for either; multifactor authentication usage is 30 days on all tiers; Microsoft Graph activity logs are unavailable on Free and on P1 and P2 are not retained at all unless archived to storage or integrated with analytics tools; risky sign-ins are 7 days on Free, 30 on P1 and 90 on P2, which is the only place the premium tier extends retention; risky users have no retention limit on any tier and risky users are not deleted until the risk has been remediated. External ID Basic plan logs are retained for 7 days. Retention changes are not retroactive: switching from free to premium shows only up to 7 days of data, and data that has already expired cannot be recovered unless it was previously archived. Collection starts at subscription sign-up on premium tiers but only when the portal or reporting API is first used on Free, and if there is no prior data it takes up to three days to appear after upgrading. Entra audit and sign-in logs are separate from the Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log, whose retention is managed through Microsoft Purview and is unaffected by Entra licensing. Provisioning logs record identity, action, source system, target system and status, with actions Create, Update, Delete, Disable, StagedDelete and Other, and statuses Success, Failure, Skipped and Warning; details are grouped into Steps, Troubleshooting and Recommendations, Modified Properties which shows old and new values, and Summary.
svg.title: Three questions, three logs, one clock — and the clock does not rewind
svg.text: P2 buys no extra days of audit or sign-in history. Thirty days, same as P1.
Sign-ins answer who got in · audit answers what changed · provisioning answers what a connector did to another system.

Risky sign-ins is the ONLY row where the premium tier extends retention. “We have P2, so we have logs” means one month.
Risky users has no limit because entries “are not deleted until the risk has been remediated” — a backlog, not a feed.
External ID Basic plan: 7 days. Same answer as post #54 reached from the other direction.
The clock does not rewind
“Log retention changes aren’t retroactive… Data that has
already expired can’t be recovered unless it was previously
archived.”
So every day without an export is a day permanently gone.
No catch-up, no backfill, no support request.
On Free, collection starts only at first portal or API use —
a tenant nobody opened is keeping nothing, not seven days.
After upgrading with no prior data: up to three days to appear.
Two audit logs, and only one is yours
“Microsoft Entra ID audit and sign-in logs are separate from
the Microsoft 365 Unified Audit Log (UAL). UAL retention is
managed through Microsoft Purview Audit and is not affected
by Microsoft Entra ID licensing changes.”
So on E5, Purview Audit (Premium) is an explicit alternative
to exporting to Azure Storage. Check it BEFORE building a
pipeline you may already be paying for.
And: only the M365 admin center shows the full M365 view.
Sign-in logs are four logs wearing one name
Interactive user · non-interactive user · service principal · managed identity. Read any entry as who (identity), how (client
application) and what (target resource) — which maps straight onto a Conditional Access policy.
“The legacy sign-in logs experience only includes interactive user sign-ins.” So “was this service principal used?” cannot be
answered there — and three of the four types are machine identities or token refreshes, where the activity often is.
Provisioning is the only log that shows you a diff
Records
identity · action · source system · target system · status
Actions
Create · Update · Delete · Disable · StagedDelete · Other
Statuses
Success · Failure · SKIPPED · Warning
Five recorded steps
import · match · determine scope · evaluate · provision
Modified Properties tab
shows “the old value and the new value” — unique in Entra
Skipped is this phase’s recurring shape, named out loud. A skipped event is not a failure and will not appear in a failure
count: the connector decided the object was out of scope and moved on. Post #50’s dropped group member and #57’s
trigger that matched nobody are the same event seen through different tools.
Reading all of this needs only Reports Reader, and entries “can’t be changed or deleted” — so delegating log access costs
no integrity risk. The one access decision in this phase that needs no deliberation at all.
Sources: Microsoft Entra data retention, Sign-in logs in Microsoft Entra ID, and User provisioning logs in Microsoft Entra ID, on Microsoft Learn.
